Programs with additional requirements
In addition to the general admission requirements, the programs listed below have extra program-specific requirements. These additional requirements must be arranged with the departments to which you are applying. It is your responsibility to make these arrangements. Please click on the names of the programs below for information about letters of intent, portfolios, interviews, auditions and specific deadline dates.

Communication (PhD)
Supervision:
While you are not required to secure a supervisor before applying, it is recommended that you reach out to potential supervisors to discuss your project and how their expertise may support your research. A supervisor match will be made at the time of admission.
Statement of purpose (approximately 500 words):
Describe your academic and/or professional background
Include any publications, awards and relevant employment
Outline your career goals
Explain why Concordia's PhD in Communication program is the right fit for your studies
If relevant, please also indicate any scholarships, fellowships or bursaries you have already secured for your PhD studies or for which you intend to apply
Research statement (approximately 1500-2000 words):
Provide a detailed description of your proposed research area(s) and program of study
Outline your research objectives and methodology
Explain the significance and potential impact of your research
If applicable, mention any theoretical frameworks or key concepts guiding your study
Bibliography: Include a one-page list of key works relevant to your proposed research area
Optional support material:
You may submit writing samples or research-creation materials as links or attachments.
Community Economic Development (GrDip)
Statement of purpose (approximately 600 words):
explain your understanding of Community Economic Development (CED)
your motivation for applying
and your relevant experiences and skills in CED or community work
Reference letters and Academic Assessment Forms:
If you have an undergraduate degree: Submit two letters of reference and academic assessment formsâone from an academic source and one from a work or volunteering source that can speak to your experience in CED.
If you don't have an undergraduate degree: Submit three letters of reference and academic assessment forms from work or volunteering sources that can speak to your CED experience and ability to pursue graduate studies.
Language requirements:
If your primary language is not English or French, submit official language test scores unless exempted. If your education was not in the language of instruction for the program you're applying to, you may need to complete a short video assessment with the program director.
Interview:
In some cases, you may be asked for an interview.

Building Engineering (MASc)
Supervision:
You may identify up to three potential faculty members in your application form. Once the application is considered complete, it will be forwarded to the department to be reviewed by potential faculty members. Although you may be selected by a Faculty member, to accelerate the process, we highly recommend that you review the list of faculty members' research interests and directly contact those whose research work aligns with yours.
An admission offer will not be issued until a supervisor match has been made.
When contacting the potential supervisors, please include the following in your email:
Your Student ID
A detailed CV (including any relevant research and work experience)
All relevant transcripts
A brief statement of your research interest and background, or a research proposal
NOTE:
To automatically be considered for the MEng (Course-Based option), in case you are not admitted to the MASc (Thesis option), check the box on the "Program Selection" page of your application.
If you did not check the box on the "Program Selection" page of your application and are not admitted to the MASc (Thesis option) but qualify for the MEng program, you will be notified and offered admission to MEng instead.
If you wish to switch from MASc (thesis-based) to MEng (course-based) at any point during the admissions process, please send a request to the Graduate Admissions team.

Program proposal (7-10 pages double-spaced) including:
a detailed statement of the fields of study and the core areas to be covered by the proposed program
a concise description of the intended research (including expected outcomes, a detailed rationale of the need for an individualized program)
a statement explaining the relationship between the proposed members of the supervisory committee and the core areas of the proposed research
a list of the four courses (12 credits) of coursework central to your project:
one methodology course (3 credits)
two regularly scheduled calendar courses (6 credits)
an independent study course with a member of your supervisory committee (3 credits)

Bibliography (two pages)
